![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253560/assets/c27074480ce1627c5f5c54596b9adaea1800bcd657a7a392c71be86b27949424.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{4}{5},$ what is the value of $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253560/assets/574143239dacf6a0eb11307826c62db531384aa03b9c0f4bade4d77c66499c23.png)

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{4}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{16}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{9}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ is negative in the second quadrant. So, $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =-\frac{3}{5}.$

Finally, knowing that $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{(-\frac{3}{5})}{(\frac{4}{5})}=-\frac{3}{4}.
$$
